presentation_revision_history.prompt: Square premium painterly mythology encyclopedia illustration of one HOBGOBLIN, specifically Puck / Robin Goodfellow transformed entirely into a HOUND as he explicitly says in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream Act 3 Scene 1. Show ONE lean lively walnut-brown hound prancing sideways across an old English woodland path at night, ready to lead strangers astray. Entire body is canine: one elongated canine head and nose, two dog ears, exactly four legs ending in four paws, one curved dog tail. No human torso, hands, facial features or clothing. The hound glances knowingly sideways with a playful alert expression, not sinister hellhound. Four paws separated clearly, tail tip visible, every part comfortably inside frame. Dark forest green leaves, old walnut tree roots, antique-gold moonlit edge light and deep rich earthy brushwork; mature detailed painterly mythological art, lively magical fairy-trickster aura expressed through pose and scene without adding invented physical traits. No wings, horns, fire, extra limbs, multiple bodies, collar, leash, owner, prey, text, border or watermark. This depicts Puck's documented animal transformation, not an ordinary human dressed as a fairy.
